description: Table 2 is a rendered data table (no micrographs, spectra or curves) listing the tensile mechanical properties of as-cast and annealed Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr low-density steel strips. Five columns are headed "Samples", "YS/MPa", "UTS/MPa", "TE/%" and "UTS × TE/GPa %". The sample column is grouped in three pairs by Cr content — 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr — each with an "as-cast" and an "annealed" row, giving six data rows of mean ± scatter values: 0Cr as-cast 836 ± 7, 972 ± 22, 35 ± 8, 34.0; 0Cr annealed 967 ± 28, 1016 ± 22, 30 ± 1, 30.5; 3Cr as-cast 642 ± 6, 943 ± 10, 38 ± 3, 35.8; 3Cr annealed 919 ± 5, 1033 ± 10, 33 ± 4, 34.1; 6Cr as-cast 718 ± 17, 1001 ± 3, 38 ± 4, 38.0; 6Cr annealed 859 ± 7, 1028 ± 15, 32 ± 4, 32.9. Read down the columns, Cr addition lowers YS from 836 MPa (0Cr as-cast) to 642-718 MPa in the Cr-containing as-cast strips, annealing raises YS in every grade (largest rise, 277 MPa, for 3Cr), and TE falls slightly on annealing. The table's key quantitative anchor is the highest UTS × TE product, 38.0 GPa %, for the as-cast 6Cr strip. The table supports the claim that Cr addition and annealing trade yield strength against total elongation in these strips. Several caption/citation values (e.g. the 131/277/141 MPa YS increments) are not printed in the table itself.

observations.observation: The table's five column headers are exactly 'Samples', 'YS/MPa', 'UTS/MPa', 'TE/%' and 'UTS × TE/GPa %'.
Six data rows are present, grouped by Cr content as 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr, each with an 'as-cast' and an 'annealed' condition.
0Cr as-cast: YS = 836 ± 7 MPa, UTS = 972 ± 22 MPa, TE = 35 ± 8 %, UTS × TE = 34.0 GPa %.
0Cr annealed: YS = 967 ± 28 MPa, UTS = 1016 ± 22 MPa, TE = 30 ± 1 %, UTS × TE = 30.5 GPa %.
3Cr as-cast: YS = 642 ± 6 MPa, UTS = 943 ± 10 MPa, TE = 38 ± 3 %, UTS × TE = 35.8 GPa %.
3Cr annealed: YS = 919 ± 5 MPa, UTS = 1033 ± 10 MPa, TE = 33 ± 4 %, UTS × TE = 34.1 GPa %.
6Cr as-cast: YS = 718 ± 17 MPa, UTS = 1001 ± 3 MPa, TE = 38 ± 4 %, UTS × TE = 38.0 GPa %.
6Cr annealed: YS = 859 ± 7 MPa, UTS = 1028 ± 15 MPa, TE = 32 ± 4 %, UTS × TE = 32.9 GPa %.
The largest tabulated UTS × TE product in the table is 38.0 GPa %, in the as-cast 6Cr row.
Within every Cr grade the annealed row has a higher YS than the as-cast row (0Cr 836→967, 3Cr 642→919, 6Cr 718→859 MPa).
Within every Cr grade the annealed row has a lower TE than the as-cast row (0Cr 35→30, 3Cr 38→33, 6Cr 38→32 %).
The caption states the table lists mechanical properties of the as-cast and annealed steel strips.

The citing text states the annealing treatment increases the yield strength of the 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips by 131 MPa, 277 MPa and 141 MPa respectively; these increments are not printed in the table but are consistent with its YS columns.
The citing text states that Cr addition significantly decreases the yield strength but has no obvious effect on the elongation of the Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C steel strip.
The citing text states that after annealing the UTS of the Cr-containing strips is higher than that of the Cr-free strip, matching the table (0Cr annealed 1016 MPa vs 3Cr 1033 MPa and 6Cr 1028 MPa).
